# PreJudge GitHub Action

Score your repo against the neatHack rubric on every push. The score, the category breakdown,
progress since the last check and the top 3 fixes land in the job's summary page.

1. Copy [`prejudge.yml`](prejudge.yml) to `.github/workflows/prejudge.yml` in your repo.
2. Push. Open the run under **Actions** and read the summary.

No secrets and no setup: it calls PreJudge's public API with your public repo URL
(`https://github.com/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY`) using `curl` and `jq`, which every Ubuntu runner has.

```
## 🔥 PreJudge: 75/100
Deep check of b2ac135 · full result
| Category | Points |  …
### Top fixes
1. Demo video (<= 3 min, covers all three tools) (+20.0 pts): Record a demo of at most 3 minutes …
```

## Behaviour

- **Never blocks your build.** Rate limited, PreJudge down, or a slow queue: it writes why to the
  summary and exits 0. To fail the job below a score, set `MIN_SCORE` (e.g. `"60"`) in the workflow.
- **Cheap on repeat pushes.** An unchanged commit returns the saved result; new commits get a quick
  audit (~15s). Deep checks are not started by the Action: run one from the result page.
- **Respects the API's limits:** 5 new audits per 10 minutes per IP (GitHub's runners share IPs, so
  a 429 can happen; the summary says so). `concurrency` cancels a superseded run on rapid pushes.
- The job has `contents: read` only and a 5-minute timeout. Nothing from your repo is executed.

Point `PREJUDGE_API` at another deployment to use your own PreJudge.

## Tested

`backend/tests/test_github_action.py` runs the workflow's exact bash step against a stub API
(success, `MIN_SCORE` gate, HTTP 429, API down). The same step was run against production for
this repo before the workflow was enabled here.

# PreJudge: get roasted before the judges do

**Live: https://3-82-224-157.sslip.io** · neatHack (Oct 10–12, 2026) · team QBITS

PreJudge is an AI agent that audits a hackathon submission before the real judges see it. Paste a
public GitHub repo URL and in about 5 seconds you get a judge-readiness score (0–100) mapped to the
official neatHack rubric, a fix list ordered by the points each fix is worth, and a short roast
that has to quote facts from your repo. Ask for the deep check and the agent downloads a read-only
copy of the repo, pulls the claims out of your README and tries to prove or disprove each one with
`file:line` evidence, then rescores. It never runs the audited code, and the README is never
accepted as proof of its own claims. The result is a shareable page with a roast card (PNG + link
preview).

> 🎬 **Demo video (≤ 3 min):** _link coming Monday, Oct 12_

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    U[Repo URL] --> Q
16:## How it works
99:## How we use neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai
139:## Evidence
199:## Building in public
203:## Run it yourself
217:## Repo layout

public GitHub repo URL and in about 5 seconds you get a judge-readiness score (0–100) mapped to the
official neatHack rubric, a fix list ordered by the points each fix is worth, and a short roast
that has to quote facts from your repo. Ask for the deep check and the agent downloads a read-only
copy of the repo, pulls the claims out of your README and tries to prove or disprove each one with
`file:line` evidence, then rescores. It never runs the audited code, and the README is never
accepted as proof of its own claims. The result is a shareable page with a roast card (PNG + link
preview).

def check_neatlogs_usage(dep_files: dict[str, str], readme: str) -> dict:
    title = "neatlogs SDK is actually used"
    rx = re.compile(r"\bneatlogs\b", re.I)
    in_deps = [p for p, txt in dep_files.items() if rx.search(txt)]
    if in_deps:
        return _check("neatlogs_sdk", "tools", title, "pass",
                      "neatlogs declared as a dependency", in_deps)
    if rx.search(readme or ""):
        return _check("neatlogs_sdk", "tools", title, "warn",
                      "README mentions neatlogs but no dependency file declares it",
                      _snippets(readme, rx, 2))
    return _check("neatlogs_sdk", "tools", title, "fail", "no sign of neatlogs in dependencies or README")


_IMAGE = re.compile(r"!\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)\s]+)|<img\b[^>]*\bsrc=[\"']([^\"']+)", re.I)
_TRACE_WORDS = re.compile(r"neatlogs|trace", re.I)
_LOGIN_PATH = re.compile(r"^/(auth|login|signin|sign-in)\b", re.I)


def trace_screenshots(readme: str, tree_paths: list[str] | None = None, links: list[dict] | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """README-embedded images whose alt text or path mentions neatlogs/trace and that actually
    exist: a relative path must be a file in the repo, a URL must not be a dead link."""
    files = {p.lower() for p in tree_paths or []}
    dead = {l["url"] for l in links or [] if l["ok"] is False}
    out = []
    for m in _IMAGE.finditer(readme or ""):
        alt, src = m.group(1) or "", m.group(2) or m.group(3) or ""
        if not (_TRACE_WORDS.search(alt) or _TRACE_WORDS.search(src)):
            continue
        if src.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
            ok = src not in dead
        else:
            ok = src.split("#")[0].split("?")[0].lstrip("./").lower() in files
        if ok:
            out.append(src)
    return out[:5]


def needs_login(link: dict) -> bool:
    """neatlogs answers a logged-out visitor with a redirect to /auth?intent=signin (or a 401)."""
    final = urlparse(link.get("final_url") or link["url"])
    return (bool(_LOGIN_PATH.search(final.path or "")) or "callbackUrl=" in (final.query or "")
            or link.get("status") == 401)

The app would first call `GET /sessions/{sessionId}`, which accepts our project API key, to find the trace ids, then post feedback to one of those traces.
  
  **(d) Caveats.**
  - **This is the blocker:** every feedback write (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, bulk) accepts only an **OAuth user token** (`nloa_` prefix, scope `observability:write`).
